nominees.name: David Huang
nominees.affiliation: Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, USA

motivation: In 1991 Fujimoto, Huang and Swanson showed that low-coherence interferometry with broadband light can produce cross-sectional images of living tissue with micrometre resolution. The technique uses the short coherence length of light to gate out echoes, much as ultrafast optics resolves events in time. OCT let physicians see what no one could see before: the layered microstructure of the living retina, without contact or ionizing radiation. Its later Fourier-domain and swept-source versions raised speed and sensitivity by orders of magnitude. Today OCT is used in tens of millions of eye examinations each year and has transformed the diagnosis of glaucoma, macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy. It is also spreading into cardiology and other areas of medicine. It is a striking example of how basic research in optical physics, in coherence and interferometry, becomes a disruptive technology that benefits society on a global scale.
